prospects.thesis: Leidos is our top-ranked prospect, combining the highest composite score with a compelling 0.8x P/S valuation and strong +15.4% monthly momentum. The company's diversified defense IT portfolio—spanning intelligence, cyber, and health mission systems—positions it to capture accelerating federal AI and digital modernization budgets. Bullish options flow and institutional accumulation confirm smart money is building positions ahead of expected FY26 contract awards.

RTX offers large-cap defense prime exposure with a differentiated missile/air defense franchise (Raytheon) benefiting from replenishment orders and elevated global threat environments. The +16.2% one-month move reflects momentum in Pratt & Whitney's GTF recovery and Patriot/LTAMDS backlog growth, while bullish options and institutional signals reinforce conviction. A rising VIX environment historically favors defense primes as defensive growth.

PATH is our preferred AI/ML pure-play, offering enterprise automation exposure at a reasonable 3.8x P/S with strong +15.7% momentum suggesting a turnaround inflection. The pivot toward agentic AI and Autopilot products is expanding TAM beyond traditional RPA, and bullish options combined with institutional buying suggest positioning ahead of an earnings catalyst. Small-cap ($6.4B) provides asymmetric upside versus mega-cap AI names on our existing watchlist.

AVAV provides differentiated unmanned systems and loitering munitions exposure (Switchblade), a sub-niche distinct from primes like RTX/LMT and directly benefiting from Ukraine/Israel demand and DoD's Replicator drone initiative. The more modest +5.3% one-month move suggests a less-extended entry versus other defense names, while bullish options flow signals informed positioning ahead of catalysts. Pure-play drone/autonomy leadership makes this a high-conviction structural growth story.

GTLB captures the AI-native DevSecOps sub-theme with GitLab Duo integrating LLM-based code assistance across its unified platform, differentiating from Microsoft/GitHub. Strong +14.3% momentum and institutional bullishness suggest re-rating potential, though 5.7x P/S demands disciplined entry. Provides small-cap software diversification distinct from PATH's automation angle and complements the watchlist's mega-cap AI exposure.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Big money is piling into Real Estate and Communication Services in a way that's hard to ignore — XLRE's put/call ratio at 0.03 is essentially a one-way bet that rates are coming down, which lines up with growing political pressure on the Fed and softening economic data giving cover for cuts, while XLC's 11x volume surge suggests traders are positioning for the AI and ad-spend narrative to keep carrying mega-cap names like Meta and Alphabet through year-end. What's more interesting is what's being dumped: Energy, Financials, and especially Consumer Staples are getting hedged aggressively, with Staples' 9.26 P/C ratio being the kind of number you rarely see — someone big is betting that either tariffs are about to squeeze margins on imported goods or that the consumer is quietly breaking, and Energy getting sold hard tells me traders think either a Russia-Ukraine deal or slowing demand is going to crush crude. The credit market is flashing a warning too — investment-grade bonds (LQD) are getting heavily hedged while junk (HYG) stays bid, which is a weird "risk-on in stocks, risk-off in safe bonds" combo that usually resolves with a volatility spike in the next 4-8 weeks.
